prompt: compare survival rates by passenger class and sex from data/raw/public/titanic.csv
checks: Both class and sex are shown. Female 1st-class survival ~97%, male 3rd-class ~14%. Large deviations suggest a blanket dropna().
final_message:
Survival was much higher for women than for men in every class, and it fell with class for both sexes. I charted it as grouped bars with sample sizes labelled.

| Class | Female | Male |
|---|---|---|
| 1st | 96.8% (91/94) | 36.9% (45/122) |
| 2nd | 92.1% (70/76) | 15.7% (17/108) |
| 3rd | 50.0% (72/144) | 13.5% (47/347) |

- **Sex:** The gap is largest in 1st and 2nd class, at about 60 and 76 percentage points. In 3rd class it is about 36 points.
- **Class:** Women in 1st and 2nd class survived at nearly the same rate (97% and 92%), but 3rd-class women survived at only 50%.
- **Men:** Only 1st-class men did notably better, at 37%. Men in 2nd and 3rd class survived at 16% and 14%.
- **Caveat:** 3rd-class men are the largest group (347), while 1st-class and 2nd-class women are small (94 and 76), so their rates are less precise.

The chart is saved at `figures/titanic_survival_class_sex.png`.
